msg: warning: Variable c is used uninitialized!
reasoning: FALSE POSITIVE: 472a474c663.c (Linux APIC). Uninitialized value on 'c' at line 12 ('static char *ptr = &c'), presence condition True. 'static char c' at line 11 is a static variable — in C, static variables are automatically zero-initialized by the runtime. Taking the address of c with '&c' does not read c's value; it only obtains a pointer to c's memory location. The alarm incorrectly identifies this as 'using c uninitialized.' The real known vbdb bug in this file is the NULL dereference on the second call to enable_IR_x2apic() (ptr is set to NULL on first call, then *ptr = 'a' dereferences NULL on second call), which requires CONFIG_SMP=true.
